mainTopic: The אגדה of אשמדאי and שלמה: the שמיר, אשמדאי's hidden knowledge, שלמה's fall and return, and a return to cures for headaches
overview: This amud continues the אגדה of אשמדאי, king of the demons, being brought in chains to שלמה המלך. On the way he spares a widow's house, helps a blind man and a drunk, cries at a wedding, and laughs at a shoemaker and a sorcerer. In ירושלים he sends coded brick messages and then rebukes שלמה. שלמה explains that he only needs the שמיר to build the בית המקדש, and his men get it by tricking the wild rooster. בניהו asks אשמדאי to explain his strange behavior, and each answer shows that he knew hidden things. Later אשמדאי tricks שלמה into giving up his ring and throws him far away. He takes his place until the חכמים expose the fake king and bring שלמה back. Finally, the גמרא returns to its list of cures, for a headache from too much blood and for a migraine.

steps.title: אשמדאי breaks a bone to spare a widow's house
steps.stepSummary: A widow begs אשמדאי not to knock down her house. He twists away from it, breaks one of his own bones, and quotes a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: She begged him not to knock down her house. He bent his body away from her and broke a bone. He said: This is what the פסוק means: 'A soft tongue can break a bone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: אשמדאי is being led along the road, and a widow pleads with him. He turns aside so hard that he breaks his own bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשמדאי is huge and powerful, yet a gentle plea moves him. He points out that this is exactly what the פסוק in משלי says: soft words can break something as hard as bone. Here the פסוק comes true almost literally.

phrases.english: She begged him.
He bent his body away from her,
and one of his bones broke.
He said: This is what is written:
"And a soft tongue breaks a bone."
phrases.notes: משלי 25:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אשמדאי being brought to שלמה from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentle plea moved אשמדאי so much that he broke his own bone, which fulfills the פסוק 'a soft tongue breaks a bone.'

steps.title: אשמדאי guides a blind man and a drunk back to the road
steps.stepSummary: On the road אשמדאי sees a blind man and then a drunk man, each lost, and puts each one back on the right path.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw a blind man who had lost his way, and he put him back on his road. He saw a drunk who had lost his way, and he put him back on his road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists more surprising things אשמדאי did on the journey. Here he helps two lost people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases match on purpose: both people are wandering off the road and both get led back. The story keeps showing an unexpected, kind side of the demon king.

keyTerms.meaning: he brought him up / put him back

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָא סַמְיָא דַּהֲוָה קָא טָעֵי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: He saw a blind man who was lost on the road,
and he brought him back to his road.

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָא רַוְיָא דַּהֲוָה קָא טָעֵי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: He saw a drunk who was lost on the road,
and he brought him back to his road.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזָא סַמְיָא דַּהֲוָה קָא טָעֵי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more episodes from the same journey.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי helped a blind man and a drunk man who were lost.

steps.title: אשמדאי cries at a wedding and laughs twice
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי cries when he sees a wedding celebration. He laughs at a man ordering shoes to last seven years, and laughs at a sorcerer doing magic.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw a wedding party celebrating, and he cried. He heard a man telling a shoemaker, 'Make me shoes that will last seven years,' and he laughed. He saw a sorcerer doing magic, and he laughed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three more strange reactions without explaining them yet. This sets up a puzzle that the story answers later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crying at a happy event and laughing at ordinary activities looks backwards. The listener is meant to wonder why. In Steps 10–19 בניהו asks about each reaction, and אשמדאי explains it.
steps.confusionAlert: The reasons for these reactions are not given here. Don't guess them yet; בניהו asks about each one, and אשמדאי explains them in Steps 10–19.

phrases.english: He saw a celebration that people were rejoicing at,
and he cried.
He heard a certain man
who was saying to a shoemaker:
Make me shoes for seven years,
and he laughed.
He saw a certain sorcerer who was doing magic,
and he laughed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of things אשמדאי did on the road, now with reactions that look strange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי cried at a wedding and laughed at a shoe order and at a sorcerer, with no reason given yet.

steps.title: First day of waiting: the brick placed on a brick
steps.stepSummary: In ירושלים, אשמדאי is kept from שלמה for three days. On the first day he is told the king drank too much. He puts one brick on top of another, and שלמה reads this as 'give him more to drink.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When he arrived there, they did not bring him to שלמה for three days. On the first day he asked: Why doesn't the king want to see me? They told him: Drink has overcome him. He took a brick and put it on top of another brick. They told שלמה, and he said: This is his message to you: Go back and give him more to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי arrives and must wait. He sends a silent message with bricks, and שלמה understands it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a brick on a brick means adding more of the same. So שלמה reads it as advice to the servants: if the king has had too much to drink, give him more. Each wise figure here talks in signs, and each one understands the other.

keyTerms.meaning: go back and give him to drink

phrases.english: When he arrived there,
they did not bring him in to Solomon
for three days.
On the first day he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי לָא קָא בָעֵי לִי מַלְכָּא לְגַבֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: Why doesn't the king want me to come to him?
They said to him: Drink has overcome him.
He took a brick and placed it on another one.
They came and told Solomon.
He said to them: This is what he told you:
Go back and give him more to drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The journey ends and the scene moves to ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי's brick on a brick meant 'give him more to drink,' and שלמה understood it.

steps.title: Second day of waiting: the brick placed on the ground
steps.stepSummary: On the next day he is told the king ate too much. He takes the brick off and puts it on the ground, and שלמה reads this as 'take his food away from him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day he asked: And why doesn't the king want to see me? They told him: Food has overcome him. He took the brick off the other one and put it on the ground. They told שלמה, and he said: This is his message to you: Take his food away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The same pattern repeats with a new excuse and a new sign. This time the sign is taking a brick away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the brick means taking something away. So for too much food the advice is the opposite of the first day: stop eating. The two days show opposite cures, drink more for drinking and less food for eating.
steps.whatToRemember: אשמדאי and שלמה talk in signs. A brick added means 'give more drink,' and a brick removed means 'take away food.'

phrases.english: The next day he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי לָא קָא בָּעֵי לִי מַלְכָּא לְגַבֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: And why doesn't the king want me to come to him?
They said to him: Food has overcome him.
He took the brick off the other one,
and placed it on the ground.
They came and told Solomon.
He said to them: This is what he told you:
Take his food away from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first day's pattern with a new excuse and the opposite sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing the brick meant 'take away his food,' and שלמה again understood it.

steps.title: אשמדאי measures four cubits and rebukes שלמה
steps.stepSummary: After three days אשמדאי comes before שלמה. He measures four cubits with a reed and tells שלמה that in the end a man owns only four cubits, yet שלמה wants to conquer even him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end of three days he came before שלמה. He took a reed, measured four cubits, and threw it in front of him. He said: When this man dies, all he will have in this world is four cubits. You have already conquered the whole world, and you are still not satisfied until you conquer me too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. אשמדאי finally meets שלמה and scolds him for his endless desire to conquer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four cubits stand for a grave, the only space a person keeps after death. אשמדאי uses this to argue that שלמה's capture of him is greed. This sets up שלמה's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubits (a unit of measure, about an arm's length)

phrases.english: At the end of three days he came in before him.
He took a reed,
and measured four cubits,
and threw it before him.
He said to him: Look,
when that man dies,
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'you'; he means שלמה himself.

phrases.english: he has nothing in this world
except four cubits;
phrases.notes: He means the space of a grave.

phrases.english: now you have conquered the whole world,
and you are not satisfied
until you conquer me as well?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the three days of waiting from Steps 4-5 with the actual meeting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person keeps only four cubits in the end, so endless conquest is pointless.

steps.title: שלמה asks for the שמיר and learns who holds it
steps.stepSummary: שלמה says he only needs the שמיר to build the בית המקדש. אשמדאי answers that he doesn't have it. The שר של ים has it, and he gives it only to the תרנגול בר, whom he trusts because of its oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה said: I don't want anything from you. I want to build the בית המקדש, and I need the שמיר. אשמדאי said: It was not given to me. It was given to the minister of the sea, and he gives it only to the wild rooster, whom he trusts because of its oath.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה explains why he captured אשמדאי, and אשמדאי tells him where the שמיר really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers אשמדאי's complaint: שלמה is not being greedy, he needs the שמיר for the בית המקדש. The trail now moves from אשמדאי to the שר של ים, and then to the תרנגול בר. The rooster's oath matters later in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The שמיר, a creature that could cut stone
The wild rooster (identified with the דוכיפת, the hoopoe)

phrases.english: He said to him:
I don't want anything from you;
I want to build the Temple,
and I need the shamir.
He said to him:
It was not handed over to me;
it was handed over to the minister of the sea;
phrases.notes: This is the angel in charge of the sea.

phrases.english: and he does not give it
except to the wild rooster,
whom he trusts on its oath.
phrases.notes: The rooster swore to give the שמיר back, so the minister trusts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שלמה answers אשמדאי's rebuke and the story moves to the search for the שמיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שמיר is with the שר של ים, who lends it only to the trusted תרנגול בר.

steps.title: What the wild rooster does with the שמיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the rooster uses the שמיר to split bare mountains and then plants tree seeds there so people can live there. This is why the תרגום calls the bird 'נגר טורא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it do with it? It brings it to mountains where no one can live, puts it on the rocky peak, and the mountain splits. Then it gathers tree seeds, throws them there, and the place becomes livable. That is why we translate the bird's name as 'cutter of the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to explain what the rooster uses the שמיר for, and ties this to a word in the תרגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'what does it do with it' is an explanation inside the story, not a challenge. The answer explains the rooster's name in the תרגום, 'נגר טורא,' which literally means 'mountain cutter.'

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people can live
The rocky crag of a mountain
Cutter of the mountain, the תרגום's name for the דוכיפת

phrases.english: And what does it do with it?
It brings it to mountains
where no one can live,
and places it on the rocky crag of the mountain,
and the mountain splits;
and it gathers and brings seeds of trees,
and throws them there,
and it becomes a place where people can live.
And this is why we translate:
"cutter of the mountain."
phrases.notes: This is how the תרגום translates the bird דוכיפת (ויקרא 11:19).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds background about the תרנגול בר mentioned in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rooster splits bare mountains with the שמיר and plants them, which explains the name נגר טורא.

steps.title: שלמה's men trick the rooster and take the שמיר
steps.stepSummary: They find the rooster's nest with chicks and cover it with clear glass. The rooster brings the שמיר to cut the glass. They startle it, it drops the שמיר, and they take it. The rooster then strangles itself for breaking its oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: They found a wild rooster's nest with chicks and covered it with clear glass. When the rooster came, it wanted to go in but couldn't. It went and brought the שמיר and set it on the glass. They threw a clump at it, it dropped the שמיר, and they took it. The rooster went and strangled itself because it had broken its oath.
steps.whatsHappening: Using what אשמדאי told them, שלמה's men trick the rooster into bringing out the שמיר and grab it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clear glass lets the rooster see its chicks but blocks it from reaching them, so it uses the שמיר to cut through. That gives the men their chance to take it. Because the rooster swore to return the שמיר (Step 7), it kills itself when it can't keep the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a clump of dirt thrown at the bird

steps.whatToRemember: The שמיר was taken through the rooster's love for its chicks. The rooster was so bound by its oath that it took its own life when it could not return the שמיר.

phrases.english: They searched out a nest of a wild rooster
that had chicks,
and covered its nest with clear glass.
When it came,
it wanted to go in but could not.
It went and brought the shamir,
and set it on top of it.
phrases.notes: It put the שמיר on the glass to cut through it.

phrases.english: He threw a clump at it,
it dropped it,
he took it.
It went and strangled itself because of its oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts on אשמדאי's information from Step 7 and finishes the search for the שמיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה's men got the שמיר by tricking the rooster, which then died over its broken oath.

steps.title: Why did you help the blind man?
steps.stepSummary: בניהו asks אשמדאי why he guided a lost blind man back to the right road.
steps.simpleTranslation: בניהו said to him: Why, when you saw that blind man lost on the road, did you bring him back to his road?
steps.whatsHappening: The story looks back at things אשמדאי did on the road to שלמה. בניהו starts asking him to explain each one, beginning with the blind man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשמדאי is a שד, so it seems odd that he would kindly help a lost blind man. The question sets up his answer in the next step, and it opens a series of five questions: the blind man, the drunk, the wedding, the shoemaker and the sorcerer.

keyTerms.meaning: בניהו בן יהוידע, the man שלמה sent to capture אשמדאי
You brought him up / set him back on his way

phrases.english: בניהו said to him:
What is the reason
that when you saw that blind man
who was lost on the road,
you brought him to his road?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to events from the journey to שלמה, so that בניהו can ask about them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אשמדאי helped a lost blind man

steps.title: The blind man is completely righteous
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי says heaven announces that the blind man is a צדיק גמור, and whoever helps him earns עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They announce about him in heaven that he is a completely righteous man, and whoever does him a kindness earns the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי answers that he knew from heaven that this blind man is a צדיק גמור, and that helping him earns a great reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשמדאי can hear what is announced in heaven, so he knows things people do not. He helped the man because helping a צדיק earns עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that pleases him / a kindness to him

phrases.english: He said to him:
They announce about him in heaven
that he is a completely righteous man,
and whoever does something that pleases him,
merits the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַכְרְזִי עֲלֵיהּ בִּרְקִיעָא דְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the blind man.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Heaven announced he is a צדיק גמור, and helping him earns עולם הבא.

steps.title: Why did you help the drunk man?
steps.stepSummary: בניהו asks why אשמדאי also guided a lost drunk man back to the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why, when you saw that drunk man lost on the road, did you bring him back to his road?
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו asks his second question. This time it is about a drunk man whom אשמדאי also helped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the last answer, we might think this drunk man was also a צדיק. The question sets up a surprising answer that is the opposite.

phrases.english: And what is the reason
that when you saw that drunk man
who was lost on the road,
you brought him to his road?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא כִּי חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְהָהוּא רַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אשמדאי helped a lost drunk man

steps.title: The drunk man is completely wicked
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי says heaven announces that the drunk man is a רשע גמור. He did him a kindness so the man would use up his reward in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They announce about him in heaven that he is a completely wicked man, and I did him a kindness so that he will use up his reward in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי explains that he helped the drunk man for the opposite reason: the man is a רשע גמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשע also gets reward for any good he has, but he gets it in this world so that nothing is left for עולם הבא. By doing him a favor now, אשמדאי helped use up his reward here.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he will 'eat up' his reward in this world

phrases.english: He said to him:
They announce about him in heaven
that he is a completely wicked man,
and I did something that pleased him
so that he will consume his world.
phrases.notes: Literally 'eat his world.' He means the man uses up his reward here, so nothing is left for later.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַכְרְזִי עֲלֵיהּ בִּרְקִיעָא דְּרָשָׁע גָּמוּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the drunk-man question. The reason is the opposite of the one in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is a רשע גמור; the favor lets him use up his reward in this world.

steps.title: Why did you cry at the wedding?
steps.stepSummary: בניהו asks why אשמדאי cried when he saw a wedding celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when you saw that celebration, did you cry?
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו asks his third question: why אשמדאי cried at a happy wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crying at a wedding is the opposite of what people normally do. The question sets up his explanation that he knew something sad was coming.

phrases.english: What is the reason
that when you saw that celebration,
you cried?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְהָהוּא חֶדְוְותָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אשמדאי cried at the wedding

steps.title: The groom will die and the bride must wait for a young יבם
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי knew the groom would die within thirty days. The bride would then have to wait thirteen years for a young brother-in-law to grow up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The man is going to die within thirty days, and she will have to wait thirteen years for a young brother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי explains that he cried because he knew the groom would soon die, leaving the bride stuck for many years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man dies without children, his widow is tied to his brother, the יבם, for יבום or חליצה. Here the brother is a קטן, so she cannot marry anyone until he grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead husband's brother, who must do יבום or חליצה
A minor, below the age of מצוות

phrases.english: He said to him:
The man is going to die
within thirty days,
and she will need to wait for a young יבם
thirteen years.
phrases.notes: She is waiting for the young brother to reach thirteen, when he is old enough to free her or marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מֵימָת גַּבְרָא בְּגוֹ תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wedding question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The groom will die in thirty days, and the bride will be stuck waiting for a minor יבם.

steps.title: Why did you laugh at the man ordering shoes?
steps.stepSummary: בניהו asks why אשמדאי laughed when a man asked a shoemaker for shoes that would last seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when you heard that man tell a shoemaker, 'Make me shoes for seven years,' did you laugh?
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו asks his fourth question, about a man ordering long-lasting shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordering strong shoes seems like a normal, sensible request. The question sets up אשמדאי's explanation of why it was funny to him.

phrases.english: What is the reason
that when you heard that man
who said to the shoemaker:
'Make me shoes for seven years,'
you laughed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי שְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אשמדאי laughed at the shoe order

steps.title: He doesn't even have seven days left
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי laughed because the man would not live even seven days, yet he wanted shoes for seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That man doesn't have seven days left, and he wants shoes for seven years?!
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי explains that he laughed because he knew the man was about to die very soon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was planning years ahead without knowing his own future. אשמדאי, who knew the truth, found the gap between the plan and reality laughable.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, each of אשמדאי's strange reactions made sense because he knew hidden things: what heaven says about people, and when they would die. The next step gives one more case, the sorcerer.

phrases.english: He said to him:
That man does not have seven days,
and he wants shoes for seven years?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the shoe question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man would die within seven days, so ordering seven-year shoes was absurd.

steps.title: Why did אשמדאי laugh at the sorcerer?
steps.stepSummary: בניהו asks the last of his questions: why אשמדאי laughed when he saw a sorcerer doing magic.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the reason that you laughed when you saw that sorcerer doing magic?
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו asks about one more strange reaction of אשמדאי. This time it is laughing at a sorcerer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier questions about the drunk man, the wedding and the shoemaker. Each time, אשמדאי reacted in a way that looked odd, and now בניהו wants the hidden reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A sorcerer, someone who does magic or tells fortunes

phrases.english: What is the reason that when you saw
that sorcerer who was doing magic,
you laughed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי חֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְהָהוּא קַסָּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the same series as Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason אשמדאי laughed at the sorcerer.

steps.title: The sorcerer was sitting on a hidden treasure
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי explains that the sorcerer was sitting on top of the king's buried treasure and did not know it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because he was sitting on the king's treasure. Let him use his magic to find out what is right underneath him!
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי answers that he laughed because the sorcerer claims to know hidden things. Yet he could not even tell that a treasure was buried under his own seat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the shoemaker case, the joke is about a person who thinks he knows a lot but misses what is right in front of him. אשמדאי can see the hidden truth, and the sorcerer cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A treasury, a place where treasure is stored

steps.whatToRemember: All of אשמדאי's strange reactions came from knowing hidden facts that people around him did not know.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because he was sitting
on the king's treasury.
Let him use his magic to find what is underneath him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דַּהֲוָה יְתֵיב אַבֵּי גַזָּא דְּמַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18 and closes the series of questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sorcerer was sitting on hidden royal treasure without knowing it, so his claim to know hidden things was laughable.

steps.title: שלמה keeps אשמדאי until the בית המקדש is built
steps.stepSummary: The story moves forward: שלמה keeps אשמדאי with him until the בית המקדש is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה kept אשמדאי with him until he built the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a transition line that moves the story to its next part. It sets up the conversation between שלמה and אשמדאי that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we heard why אשמדאי was brought and how he behaved on the way. Now the story jumps ahead to the time after the building work, when the trouble begins.

phrases.english: He kept him with him
until he built the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְחֵיהּ גַּבֵּיהּ עַד דְּבַנְיֵיהּ לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the series of questions and moves the story forward in time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי stayed with שלמה until the בית המקדש was complete.

steps.title: שלמה asks what makes demons greater than people
steps.stepSummary: Alone with אשמדאי, שלמה quotes a פסוק that seems to praise demons and asks in what way they are greater than humans.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day שלמה was standing alone with him. He said to him: It is written, 'Like the lofty horns of the wild ox for him.' We explain that 'lofty horns' means the ministering angels and 'wild ox' means the demons. In what way are you greater than us?
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה asks אשמדאי a question. Since a פסוק speaks of demons as powerful, what makes them greater than people?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as speaking of angels and demons, so it seems demons have a special power. שלמה, who controls אשמדאי, wonders what that power could be. This question opens the door for אשמדאי's trick.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild ox, here read as demons

phrases.english: One day he was standing alone with him.
He said to him: It is written:
"Like the lofty horns of the wild ox for him";
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:8

phrases.english: and we say: "Like the lofty horns" means the ministering angels,
"the wild ox" means the demons.
In what way are you greater than us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The scene set up in Step 20 now begins with שלמה's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What special power demons have over human beings.

steps.title: אשמדאי tricks שלמה and throws him far away
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי gets שלמה to remove the chain and hand over his ring. Then he swallows the ring, grows huge, and flings שלמה 400 פרסאות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Take the chain off me and give me your ring, and I will show you my greatness. שלמה took the chain off him and gave him his ring. אשמדאי swallowed it, placed one wing in the sky and one wing on the earth, and threw שלמה four hundred פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי answers by showing his power instead of explaining it. Once he is free and has the ring, he overpowers שלמה and throws him far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain and the ring were what kept אשמדאי under control. When שלמה gives them up, אשמדאי's full strength comes out. The answer to 'what is your greatness' is shown, not told.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a large measure of distance

phrases.english: He said to him: Take the chain off me,
and give me your ring,
and I will show you my greatness.
He took the chain off him,
and gave him his ring.
He swallowed it,
placed one of his wings in the sky,
and one of his wings on the earth,
and threw him four hundred parasangs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שלמה's question by showing his power.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Once free of the chain and holding the ring, אשמדאי overpowers שלמה and throws him far away.

steps.title: שלמה's words at that moment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects a פסוק in קהלת to this moment: what does a person gain from all his work?
steps.simpleTranslation: About that moment שלמה said: 'What profit does a person have from all his toil that he toils under the sun?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that a famous פסוק in קהלת was said about this exact moment, when שלמה lost everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק now gets a real-life background. שלמה had been a great king, and suddenly all his work seemed worth nothing, so he asked what a person really gains.

phrases.english: About that moment Solomon said:
"What profit is there for a person from all his toil
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:3

phrases.english: that he toils under the sun?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links a פסוק to the event of Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'מה יתרון לאדם' was said when שלמה was thrown from his kingdom.

steps.title: What does 'and this' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another פסוק in קהלת and asks what the word 'וזה' ('and this') points to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And this was my portion from all my toil.' What is 'and this'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק from קהלת and asks what thing שלמה was pointing to when he said 'this.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This' sounds like שלמה is pointing at something real that he still had. After losing his kingdom, the question is what was left in his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: And this (as if pointing to something)

phrases.english: "And this was my portion from all my toil" –
phrases.notes: קהלת 2:10

phrases.english: What is "and this"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading פסוקים in קהלת against the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object the word 'וזה' refers to.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: his staff or his cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree. One says 'this' was שלמה's staff, and the other says it was his cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: one said, his staff; and one said, his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give answers. All שלמה had left from his whole kingdom was one simple item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They disagree only about which item it was. Both agree that 'this' points to the one small thing he still held after losing everything.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree;
one said: his staff;
and one said: his cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וזה' refers to the single item שלמה had left: his staff according to one view, his cloak according to the other.

steps.title: שלמה wanders, saying 'I was king'
steps.stepSummary: שלמה goes from door to door, and everywhere he says, 'I, קהלת, was king over ישראל in ירושלים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He went around from door to door. Wherever he came, he said: 'I, קהלת, was king over ישראל in ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. שלמה is now a poor wanderer, and he keeps telling people that he used to be king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the past tense 'הייתי' ('I was') to mean that שלמה was no longer king when he said it. This line sets up the reaction of the סנהדרין in the next step.

phrases.english: He would go around from door to door.
Wherever he arrived, he said:
"I, Kohelet, was king
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:12

phrases.english: over Israel in Jerusalem."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes שלמה's life after being thrown out, building on Steps 22 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה wandered as a beggar and kept declaring that he had been king.

steps.title: The סנהדרין wonder about the wanderer
steps.stepSummary: When שלמה reaches the סנהדרין, the חכמים notice that a crazy person does not stick to one idea, so they ask what is going on.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came to the סנהדרין, the חכמים said: A crazy person does not stick to one single thing. So what is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים start to suspect that this beggar might really be שלמה. A madman would jump from idea to idea, but this man always says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reasoning is simple: a person who is really a שוטה does not stay fixed on one claim. Because this man always repeats the same claim, they ask whether he might be telling the truth. This question sets up the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A crazy or mentally unstable person

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying he is crazy. They are saying the opposite: his steady, repeated claim is a sign he may not be crazy at all.

phrases.english: When he arrived at the Sanhedrin,
the Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי שׁוֹטֶה – בַּחֲדָא מִילְּתָא לָא סְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Now, a crazy person does not stick to one matter,
so what is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי שׁוֹטֶה בַּחֲדָא מִילְּתָא לָא סְרִיךְ, מַאי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to שלמה's repeated claim in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wanderer who claims to be שלמה is actually telling the truth.

steps.title: The חכמים question בניהו
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask בניהו whether the king still calls him close, and he says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked בניהו: Does the king ask you to come be with him? He said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים start investigating who is really sitting on the throne. They begin by asking בניהו, the king's right-hand man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בניהו was the king's closest helper, so a real שלמה would want him nearby. His answer is 'no,' which tells us the 'king' is keeping away from the person most likely to spot a fake. This is the first clue.

keyTerms.meaning: בניהו בן יהוידע, שלמה's top officer
to be with him, close to him

phrases.english: They said to Benayahu:
Does the king ask for you to be with him?
phrases.notes: They want to know if the king still keeps his closest helper near him, the way the real שלמה did.

phrases.english: He said to them: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים begin to act on the suspicion raised in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the king behaving normally toward his closest helper?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, the king does not call בניהו to be with him.

steps.title: The sages ask the queens and want his feet checked
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask the queens whether the king visits them and ask them to check his feet, but he always wears socks.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to the queens: Does the king come to you? The queens answered: Yes, he comes. The חכמים sent: Check his feet. The queens answered: He comes in socks.
steps.whatsHappening: The investigation goes on. The חכמים ask the king's wives for more information and try to get a look at his feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The queens confirm that the king does visit them. The feet test was meant to show whether the king is really human. The socks block the test, so the feet give no answer, and the sages are left needing another clue.

phrases.english: They sent to the queens:
Does the king come to you?
They sent back to them: Yes, he comes.
They sent to them: Check his feet.
They sent back to them: He comes in socks;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After asking בניהו, the sages question a second group, the queens.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the king visit the queens, and are his feet human?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He does visit them, but he always wears socks, so his feet cannot be checked.

steps.title: The queens report forbidden behavior
steps.stepSummary: The queens say the king asks them to be with him during נדה and even asks for בת שבע, his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he asks them to be with him when they are נדה, and he even asks for בת שבע, his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The queens give the clue that settles the question. The 'king' is doing things the real שלמה would never do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The feet test failed, but this behavior proves the case. A תורה-loyal king like שלמה would never ask for forbidden relations. This shows the man on the throne is a fake.

phrases.english: And he demands them when they are menstruating;
and he also demands
Bathsheba, his mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The queens keep reporting. This time they give the clue that answers the sages' question.
steps.raayaObject: That the king on the throne is not really שלמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The queens' report of forbidden demands that the real שלמה would never make

steps.title: שלמה returns and אשמדאי flees
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים bring the real שלמה, give him a ring and a chain carved with the שם, and אשמדאי flies away when he sees him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought שלמה and gave him a ring and a chain with the שם carved on it. When he came in, אשמדאי saw him and flew away.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the fake is exposed, the sages bring back the real שלמה and arm him. אשמדאי runs away as soon as he sees him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, אשמדאי got his power by taking שלמה's ring with the שם on it. Now שלמה gets that kind of protection again. That is why אשמדאי cannot stay and flees.

phrases.english: They brought Solomon,
and they gave him a ring,
and a chain on which the Name was carved.
When he entered, he saw him and flew away.
phrases.notes: The one who saw and flew away is אשמדאי, who sees שלמה coming in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the fake is proven, the sages act to bring back the real king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the ring and the chain of the שם, שלמה returns and אשמדאי flees.

steps.title: שלמה stays afraid, as the פסוק says
steps.stepSummary: Even after אשמדאי fled, שלמה was still afraid of him. The גמרא reads a פסוק in שיר השירים about guards around שלמה's bed this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, שלמה was afraid of him. That is what the פסוק means: 'Here is שלמה's bed, with sixty mighty men around it from the mighty men of ישראל. All of them hold swords and are trained in war, each man with his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the nights.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that שלמה's fear did not go away. It brings a פסוק about armed guards around his bed to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the sixty warriors stood guard 'because of fear in the nights.' The גמרא explains this fear as fear of אשמדאי. So the story explains why a peaceful king like שלמה needed guards at night.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written
because of fear in the nights

phrases.english: And even so,
he was afraid of him.
phrases.notes: שלמה was afraid of אשמדאי.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"Behold the bed of Solomon,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 3:7–8

phrases.english: sixty mighty men around it,
from the mighty men of Israel.
All of them hold the sword,
trained in war,
each man with his sword on his thigh
because of fear in the nights."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds what happened after אשמדאי fled and ties it to a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That שלמה stayed afraid of אשמדאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 3:7–8, about armed guards 'because of fear in the nights'

steps.title: Did שלמה ever become king again?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue about the end of the story. One says שלמה went from king to commoner, and the other says he went from king to commoner and back to king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One says: king, then commoner. The other says: king, then commoner, then king again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with an argument between רב and שמואל about how שלמה's life ended up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says that after שלמה became a commoner, he never went back to being king. The second view says he went back to his throne and became king again.
steps.whatToRemember: The fake king was exposed through his forbidden behavior, not through the failed feet test. Even after his comeback שלמה stayed afraid, and רב and שמואל argue whether he ever truly became king again.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. Both agree שלמה went from king to commoner. They only argue about whether he became king again afterward.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel:
one said: a king and then a commoner;
and one said: a king, then a commoner, and then a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר: מֶלֶךְ וְהֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the שלמה story with a disagreement about the result, much like רב and שמואל's argument in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: שלמה was king and then a commoner. The other view: king, commoner, and then king again.

steps.title: A cure for a headache from too much blood in the head
steps.stepSummary: For a headache caused by too much blood in the head, boil seven kinds of plants together and pour three hundred cups of the water on each side of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a headache from too much blood in the head: bring cypress, willow, fresh myrtle, olive, poplar, sea willow and cynodon grass. Boil them all together. Pour three hundred cups on one side of the head and three hundred cups on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of שלמה and אשמדאי is over, and the גמרא goes back to its list of cures. It gives a cure for a headache that comes from too much blood in the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cure has three parts: gather seven specific plants, boil them together, and pour a large amount of the liquid, three hundred cups, on each side of the head. Both sides get the same amount, so the whole head is treated evenly.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'blood of the head'; a headache caused by too much blood

phrases.english: For blood of the head – let him bring cypress,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to its list of cures. 'Blood of the head' means a headache that comes from too much blood there.

phrases.english: willow, fresh myrtle, olive,
poplar, sea willow, and cynodon grass;
and let him boil them together;

phrases.aramaic: וְלִנְטוֹל תְּלָת מְאָה כָּסֵי אַהַאי גִּיסָא דְרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: and let him pour three hundred cups on this side of the head,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְלָת מְאָה כָּסֵי אַהַאי גִּיסָא דְרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: and three hundred cups on this side of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שלמה and אשמדאי story and goes back to the list of medical remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven plants boiled together, and three hundred cups of the liquid poured on each side of the head, cure a headache caused by too much blood.

steps.title: A simpler backup cure with a white rose
steps.stepSummary: If the first cure is not possible, boil a white rose that grows alone and pour sixty cups on each side of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, let him bring a white rose that grows alone in its row and boil it. He should pour sixty cups on one side of the head and sixty cups on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, backup cure for the same headache, in case the first one is not an option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure is much simpler than the first. Instead of seven plants there is one special plant, a white rose growing by itself, and instead of three hundred cups on each side there are only sixty. The pattern of treating both sides of the head equally stays the same.

phrases.english: And if not – let him bring a white rose
that stands in one row, and let him boil it,
phrases.notes: 'In one row' means the rose is growing all by itself.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִינְטוֹל שִׁיתִּין כָּסֵי אַהַאי גִּיסָא דְרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: and let him pour sixty cups on this side of the head,
and sixty cups on this side of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a backup cure for the same headache described in Step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first cure is not possible, a boiled white rose growing alone, with sixty cups poured on each side of the head, can be used instead.

steps.title: A cure for a migraine with a wild rooster
steps.stepSummary: For a migraine, slaughter a wild rooster with a silver coin so its blood flows over the side of the head that hurts, avoid getting the blood in the eye, and hang the rooster on the doorpost so he brushes against it going in and out.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a migraine: bring a wild rooster and slaughter it with a silver coin over the side of the head that hurts. Be careful that the blood does not get in his eye and blind him. Then hang the rooster on the doorpost, so that whenever he goes in or out he rubs against it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new illness, a migraine, a pain on one side of the head, and gives its cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the headache cures, which treat both sides of the head, this cure targets only the side that hurts, since a migraine is on one side. The גמרא adds a safety warning about the blood and the eye. It also adds a last step: hanging the rooster where he will keep touching it every time he passes the door.

keyTerms.meaning: Migraine; pain on one side of the head

steps.whatToRemember: After the story of שלמה and אשמדאי, the גמרא is back to its list of cures: a seven-plant cure and a white-rose backup for a headache from too much blood, and a wild-rooster cure for a migraine.

phrases.english: For a migraine – let him bring a wild rooster;
and let him slaughter it with a silver coin –
phrases.notes: Literally 'a white זוז', meaning a silver coin.

phrases.english: over that side that hurts him,
and let him be careful of its blood so it does not blind his eye;
and let him hang it on the doorpost –

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי עָיֵיל חָיֵיף בֵּיהּ, וְכִי נָפֵיק חָיֵיף בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: so that when he enters he rubs against it, and when he exits he rubs against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cures, moving from a general headache to a migraine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wild rooster slaughtered with a silver coin over the painful side of the head, then hung on the doorpost to be rubbed against when going in and out, cures a migraine.
